prompt: A Cortex-M4 board runs a SysTick interrupt producer that pushes bytes from a compiled-in burst corpus into a fixed 32-byte ring while the main loop pops bytes and decodes 0x02 <length> <payload> <xor checksum> 0x03 frames. The shipped ring.c detects a full ring and drops the byte without counting it, so when the consumer falls behind, the decoder loses framing and nothing in the run explains the loss. Implement ring_init/ring_push/ring_pop/ring_overflows in ring.c so the ring stays consistent across 30 wraps of the index, every byte is either delivered or rejected and counted (pushed - popped == overruns), a fresh boot starts from a clean ring, and the interrupt handler stays inside its cycle budget. The harness sets two knobs before each boot: rate.txt is the bytes pushed per interrupt and slow.txt is a busy-wait the consumer runs between drains; the interrupt duration is clocked from the SysTick current-value register.

requirements: real SysTick interrupt producer on an emulated Cortex-M4 with a compiled-in 120-frame burst corpus
fixed 32-byte ring forcing about 30 index wraps across the corpus
rate knob (bytes per interrupt) and a consumer slow-down knob that provably overflows the ring
framed byte stream with a checksum the guest recomputes, plus explicit overrun telemetry (pushed, popped, overruns)
interrupt duration measured from the SysTick current-value register against a 400-cycle budget
paired same-model skill/no-skill execution from the identical starting snapshot
